senses.head: accompany
senses.def: To go along with; to be together.
senses.sent: A clap of thunder will usually ____ a flash of lightning by a second or two.

senses.head: accompany
senses.def: To play a musical instrument for or with.
senses.sent: The pianist offered to ____ the singer for the last song of the evening.

senses.head: beneficial
senses.def: Being of use; helpful; favorable.
senses.sent: Half an hour of walking a day is ____ to almost everyone, whatever their age.

senses.head: captive
senses.def: One that is held prisoner.
senses.sent: Every ____ taken in the raid was brought back to the fort and guarded.

senses.head: captive
senses.def: Unable to escape or get away.
senses.sent: The patients in the waiting room made a ____ audience for the man with the guitar.

senses.head: captive
senses.def: The state of being held against one's will; loss of freedom.
senses.sent: The giant panda has bred more successfully in ____ than anyone expected.

senses.head: convenient
senses.def: Suitable for one's needs; making life easier or more comfortable.
senses.sent: The bus stop is ____ for us because it is at the end of our own street.

senses.head: convenient
senses.def: Anything that makes life easier or more comfortable.
senses.sent: The apartment had air-conditioning, a lift and every other ____ we could have asked for.

senses.head: ecstasy
senses.def: A strong feeling of emotion, especially joy.
senses.sent: The crowd screamed in ____ the moment the band walked onto the stage.

senses.head: ecstasy
senses.def: Full of or causing overwhelming joy.
senses.sent: The winners were ____ when the judges finally read out their names.

senses.head: expanse
senses.def: A wide, open area or surface; a stretch.
senses.sent: From the top of the dune there was nothing but a grey ____ of water to the horizon.

senses.head: expedition
senses.def: A long journey by a group to explore or do battle.
senses.sent: Three ships and ninety men set out on an ____ to find the source of the river.

senses.head: expedition
senses.def: A group that travels together to explore or do battle.
senses.sent: By the second winter the ____ had lost two of its sledges and half its dogs.

senses.head: inept
senses.def: Clumsily or awkwardly expressed; not suitable for the occasion.
senses.sent: That ____ remark about her cooking upset everyone who overheard it.

senses.head: inept
senses.def: Lacking in skill or ability.
senses.sent: An ____ handler dropped the crate and ruined everything that was inside it.

senses.head: interpret
senses.def: To translate into another language.
senses.sent: A woman from the embassy was hired to ____ the minister's remarks for the audience.

senses.head: interpret
senses.def: To explain the meaning of.
senses.sent: Josef offered to ____ the dream for her, though she was not sure she wanted to know.

senses.head: interpret
senses.def: To understand in one's own way.
senses.sent: The coach chose to ____ my absence from the meeting as a lack of commitment.

senses.head: invaluable
senses.def: Too valuable to measure; priceless.
senses.sent: Her knowledge of the old maps turned out to be ____ once the search began.

senses.head: linger
senses.def: To be slow in leaving or going away.
senses.sent: A few guests always ____ by the door long after everyone else has gone home.

senses.head: retrieve
senses.def: To get back; to recover.
senses.sent: You can ____ anything you leave behind from the office by the gate.

senses.head: retrieve
senses.def: To find and bring back.
senses.sent: The puppy will ____ a stick from the pond all afternoon if you let her.

rounds.name: Verbs with more than one job
rounds.blurb: Two verbs that each do several things. One of them is on this list three times over — count the meanings before you start.

rounds.name: Held, and got back
rounds.blurb: The prisoner, the condition he is kept in, and the word for fetching something back again.

rounds.name: Worth having
rounds.blurb: Helpful, handy and priceless — and the noun that goes with the handy one.

rounds.name: Overjoyed, or out of your depth
rounds.blurb: The noun for great joy, the adjective made from it, and the word for doing a thing badly.

rounds.name: Open country and long journeys
rounds.blurb: A wide stretch of land or water, a journey across it, and what some people do instead of leaving.
